kept.heading: GPT-6.2 ASTRA APPEARS IN CODEX USAGE AHEAD OF POSSIBLE LAUNCH (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: GPT-6.2-Astra has started appearing in Codex usage breakdowns. The requests are likely being quietly routed to the new model as part of an A/B test or a staged rollout. A public launch could be days away. OpenAI reportedly decided to skip GPT-6.1 Astra due to concerns about deception and scope.

kept.heading: CLAUDE INTRODUCES MESSAGE THREADS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic released message threads in public beta, allowing agents to send only new messages instead of resending their entire conversation history. The feature reduced median time to first token by approximately 35% for requests with 500K–1M tokens, without changing token usage.

kept.heading: ANTHROPIC WARNS IT MAY BE CLOSE TO SELF-IMPROVING AI (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic disclosed in its updated IPO filing that it may soon reach its internal definition of recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AI systems help develop increasingly capable AI models.

kept.heading: THE HITCHHIKER'S GUIDE TO TRAINING ON COMPUTE ISLANDS (18 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Being able to train reliably on multiple smaller clusters widens the usable training pool for frontier training. A single run could mix accelerator generations and vendors as each island runs on its own schedule. Older generations or less common chips could also participate in a frontier run. One risk with this model is that integrity and safety may become harder when models are trained across providers, as one faulty or compromised site can quietly degrade or tamper with models in ways that are harder to trace.

kept.heading: HOW TO TRAIN A SWARM (19 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Swarms are AI systems where multiple agents cooperate towards a shared goal. This post discusses a technique called collective inference-time scaling, where agents scale the amount of useful work performed in parallel and the communication needed to achieve it. It also explains how to design incentives for parallel work, and covers the general topic of designing incentives for reinforcement learning.

kept.heading: LESSONS FROM BUILDING COPILOT COWORK (21 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Microsoft's Copilot Cowork, an AI-driven agentic execution layer, achieved global availability in four and a half months, switching its runtime from Python to Rust while live. Key practices included writing clear specs before coding, running narrow agents with clear boundaries, and ensuring automated checks genuinely verify code changes. The transition to Rust improved efficiency and highlighted the importance of clear testing, boundary setting, and human oversight in the development process.

kept.heading: GPU-ACCELERATED WEIGHT TELEPORTATION (17 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: GPU-accelerated Weight Teleportation optimizes RL training by improving weight syncing between trainers and samplers, reducing pause times to under 0.23 seconds. This is achieved using a co-designed compression/decompression pipeline with GPU-accelerated parallel processing, utilizing efficient codecs like LZ4 and Snappy, combined with a Zstd layer.

kept.heading: HARNESS 2: EXECUTING AGENT CODE AS IT STREAMS (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Framer's Harness 2 significantly upgrades the agent's execution process, allowing entire workflows in one program, achieving up to 33% cost reduction and 20% faster execution. This is done by executing JavaScript as it streams in, avoiding multiple model calls and using eager execution and early cancellation to enhance efficiency. The redesign also replaces DSL with method calls for real-time updates, making task execution streamlined for both in-app and external agents, reducing tool steps by 43% and cached input tokens by 39% per message.

kept.heading: NVIDIA'S COSMOS FRAMEWORK (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: NVIDIA introduced new Cosmos Framework capabilities for training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and optimizing world models for physical AI. Developers can generate synchronized video and LiDAR simulations for robotics and autonomous vehicles, then deploy models through GPU-accelerated Cosmos NIM microservices.

kept.heading: OPENAI IS FINALLY MERGING CHATGPT'S CHAT AND WORK TABS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI plans to merge the Chat and Work tabs within the ChatGPT experience after an initial testing period with select users. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app. The change will enable users to move from exploring ideas to having the chatbot complete work within the same space. Users can import files and plugins. Both ChatGPT and Codex will soon draw from the same allowance pool.

kept.heading: LLMS ARE NOT SUPERHUMAN AT READING AND WRITING NEURAL NETWORK WEIGHTS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A recent paper demonstrates GPT-6 Astra's ability to interact with neural network weights directly, surpassing human or conventional algorithm capabilities. Astra significantly improved a 0.8B Qwen LLM's mathematical skills by editing weights natively. While impressive, these capabilities reflect advanced problem-solving akin to skilled human researchers, not radically new AI capabilities.

kept.heading: ANTHROPIC RELEASES AMENDED IPO PROSPECTUS WITH THIRD-QUARTER FINANCIALS (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic's amended IPO prospectus reveals a 1,200% increase in revenue to $33.24 billion for the first nine months of 2026. The company reported a net loss of $104 billion for the same period. Anthropic's commitments for compute and infrastructure total approximately $895.4 billion.

kept.heading: LIMIT WHAT AGENTS LEARN ABOUT PRIVATE REPOS WITH ENCLAVES (17 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Enclaves are a new security primitive for cross-repository GitHub Agentic Workflows that lets agents work on different repositories while limiting what they say to each other.

kept.heading: OPENAI INTRODUCES LIFEVAL TO MEASURE AI PERFORMANCE ON EVERYDAY TASKS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: LifeVal is a benchmark designed to evaluate AI performance on practical everyday tasks such as budgeting, finding childcare, and accessing government services.

kept.heading: ELON MUSK LIMITS GROK BOT USAGE OVER RISING COSTS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Elon Musk confirmed that Grok Bot usage limits were reduced after operating costs became unsustainably high relative to revenue.

kept.heading: TEACHING QWEN WHY (47 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The research extends Anthropic's "Teaching Claude Why" methods to new models, focusing on reducing agentic misalignment through synthetic document finetuning (SDF) and supervised finetuning (SFT) with fictional stories and ethical dilemmas.

kept.heading: SIRI AI IS NOW OPEN TO ALL DEVELOPERS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Developers can now integrate Siri AI into their apps with the iOS 27.3 beta. This update allows apps to leverage Siri's advanced features, like natural language processing and personal context understanding, enhancing user interaction. Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU and for users under 13. It supports multiple languages, with more to come.

kept.heading: BASETEN INTRODUCES GRID, SANDBOXES, AND SERVERLESS LOOPS (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Baseten announced Grid for model routing and governance, resumable VM-isolated Sandboxes for agent execution, and general availability of Loops for serverless supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. The products connect training, inference, and execution, with customers retaining ownership of trained weights.

kept.heading: FIREWORKS LAUNCHES FASTER AI INFERENCE AND ENTERPRISE TOOLS (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Fireworks AI unveiled new products at Forge, including Ultra-fast inference reaching up to 1,500 tokens per second, lower-cost background processing, and Nexus for accessing multiple AI models within existing tools. It also introduced capabilities for model evaluation, fine-tuning deployment, and enterprise-controlled infrastructure.

kept.heading: HOW MUCH DOES REASONING EFFORT AFFECT SCORE AND COST? (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Lower reasoning effort reduces cost much more than it lowers the quality of results. Tests show that models on low reasoning can match models on high reasoning at lower cost. The impact of reasoning effort depends on the task.

kept.heading: TRAINING A TEXT-TO-IMAGE MODEL FOR $21K (13 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Linium is a two-person research lab that is trying to train its own generative video models entirely from scratch, aiming to create tools to democratize access to animation. Pyramid-JiT (P-JiT) is a pixel-space architecture that achieves aggressive token reduction through a noise schedule that helps pixel-space models better learn fine-grained detail. This study looks at how models trained on the architecture perform when trained for longer as a pressure test along the way towards larger models and video. Examples of images generated by the resulting model are available.

kept.heading: LEARNINGS FROM AUDITING PUBLIC EVALUATIONS (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The article outlines issues faced during public evaluations of LLMs and details improvements made to benchmarks such as AUTOMATIONBENCH and OFFICEQA PRO V2. They replaced ambiguous prose descriptions with JSON schemas for better performance evaluations and introduced new grading systems to improve accuracy. A multi-layered monitoring system is suggested to prevent manipulation and ensure accurate measurement of model capabilities.

kept.heading: GEMINI NOTEBOOK API (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The Gemini Notebook API is a REST interface for programmatically creating and managing notebooks and sources in Gemini Notebook. It can turn web pages, YouTube videos, plain text, and Markdown into persistent notebooks. The API and MCP server are in an early access Public Preview. Only personal Google Accounts are supported during the preview - Google Workspace accounts are not yet supported.

kept.heading: PROGRESS ON PROVABLE INFERENCE FOR LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (30 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: It is almost impossible to verify which model produced a specific output. Cryptographic proofs of inference allow model providers to prove that preach suppose was produced which a specific model. These proofs could enable new applications and contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements. This post details the progress made on a powerful type of cryptographic proof uniquely fit for provable inference called zKSNARK.

kept.heading: ACCELERATING ENGINEERING FOR THE PHYSICAL WORLD (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI is leveraging its AI models to enhance mechanical and electrical engineering processes, from design to simulation and production, speeding up internal workflows and improving industry practices. Engineers utilize models like GPT‑6 Astra for tasks such as device design, CAD model creation, and performance simulations, while collaborating with companies like Mazda to explore applications in vehicle aerodynamics.

kept.heading: DEEPSEEK PLANS TO TRAIN ITS NEXT-GENERATION MODEL ON HUAWEI ASCEND CHIPS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: DeepSeek plans to use Huawei's Ascend AI chips to pretrain DeepSeek V5. Ascend chips have previously been used primarily for inference rather than pretraining. This will be an important test of whether Chinese AI accelerators can support the full pre-training of a frontier large language model. A successful run could reduce Chinese AI developers' dependence on Nvidia hardware and strengthen Huawei's position as an alternative for advanced AI computing.

kept.heading: OPENAI: CHATGPT SEARCH IS ABOUT 20% OF GOOGLE'S, 250 MILLION PEOPLE SPEAK WITH CHATGPT, AND CHAT IS MERGING WITH WORK (16 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: ChatGPT's search volume has reached 20% of Google's, with ChatGPT rapidly gaining 200 million users in the past two months, leading to 1.2 billion weekly active users. The voice mode of ChatGPT now engages 250 million weekly active users, emphasizing new interaction methods through GPT Live updates that enable natural bidirectional conversations. Plans to merge Chat and Work modes aim to simplify user interaction, while Dots highlights innovations in AI task management despite high compute costs.

kept.heading: AGENT STATE MACHINES: BUILDING DETERMINISTIC SCAFFOLDING FOR AGENTS (9 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: This post explains how state machines enforce agent permissions, approvals, retries, and completion criteria outside model prompts.

kept.heading: CHATGPT IS ABOUT TO START MAKING GIFS (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI just merged animated GIF output into its image generation, with the animations being generated by OpenAI's Images API, which means it is coming to ChatGPT.

kept.heading: THE 'ASTRA CAN READ AND WRITE WEIGHTS TO IMPROVE QWEN' POST IS MISLEADING (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The 'Astra can read and write weights' claims are misleading.

kept.heading: HOW MUCH DO TOKENS REALLY COST? (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI tokens' pricing appears sustainable, as competition among providers is driving down costs.

kept.heading: OPENAI LAUNCHES IMAGES 2.6 WITH GIFS AND IMAGE REFERENCE (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI is rolling out Images 2.6 globally in ChatGPT and Codex. The new model generates images 50% faster than the previous iteration, and it can also create GIFs. Users can adjust the speed of the GIF, edit individual frames, and share it. GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst are now available through the API.

kept.heading: INTRODUCING PANGRAM IMAGE 1.0 (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Pangram Image 1.0 is an AI image and AI video detection model that can produce a heatmap localizing exactly where AI appears in images. It is robust to edits, compression, and low resolutions. There is a Chrome Extension available that can detect AI, as well as API support for images and video.

kept.heading: RIPPLE-65B PREVIEW (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Ripple-65B Preview is a frontier open-weight model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on TerminalBench 2.1. It surpasses significantly larger open-weight models from the US, including Reflection Beam 501B, Meta Muse Spark Open 816B, Thinking Machines Inkling 975B, and Nvidia Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B. The model was trained for only $32 million, one-tenth the estimated cost of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding. Ripple-65B Preview is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, and OpenRouter.

kept.heading: HOW OPENAI PATCHED 948 LINUX VULNERABILITIES (12 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI developed an autonomous pipeline for discovering, exploiting, and patching security vulnerabilities. In a single run, its cybersecurity model validated and generated patches for 948 Linux local privilege escalation vulnerabilities.

kept.heading: THE STACKS PROJECT, FORMALIZED IN LEAN (13 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Axiom has released a Lean formalization of the entire Stacks Project. The Stacks project is an open-source reference that lays the foundation of modern algebraic geometry. The release is the largest integrated, reusable library of formalized mathematics ever built. It makes the full mathematical development of the Stacks Project available as a single, machine-checked library that researchers and AI agents can import from directly into new formal proofs.

kept.heading: COGNITION INTRODUCES SWE-2 FLASH (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: SWE-2 Flash is a coding model that uses a new mid-training stage before reinforcement learning.

kept.heading: TENCENT LAUNCHES HY4, JOINING THE RANKS OF THE WORLD'S LEADING OPEN-SOURCE AI MODELS (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Hy4 is a large language model with visual understanding capabilities. Tencent plans to release model weights and system cards for the model in the coming days. The model supports a broad range of tasks that include fine-grained image processing, complex chart analysis, and mathematical visual reasoning. It can interact with both command-line interfaces and GUIs to perform a wide range of work and everyday tasks.

kept.heading: ALPHAEVOLVE (GITHUB REPO)
kept.blurb: AlphaEvolve is a Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms. It pairs the creative problem-solving capabilities of Gemini models with automated evaluators that verify answers. The agent has been used to enhance the efficiency of Google's data centers, chip design, and AI training process. This repository contains a minimal implementation of AlphaEvolve along with code and data related to solutions and discoveries it has contributed to.

kept.heading: H-NETS LEARN DIRECTLY FROM RAW BYTES (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Cartesia's H-Nets learn directly from raw bytes, matching benchmark performance with substantially less training compute.

kept.heading: OPENAI TO ACQUIRE PIERRE COMPUTER COMPANY, INC. (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company to enhance Codex's developer tools, including Code Storage and other open-source projects.

kept.heading: META ACQUIRES AI CODING STARTUP CONDUCTOR (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Conductor is a startup that lets developers run multiple AI coding agents in parallel workspaces.

kept.heading: REGISTER NOW
CAT WU JOINS OPENAI (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Cat Wu has joined OpenAI to build reliable agents that keep users in control.

kept.heading: TOGETHER COMPILER: CONTINUAL COMPILATION FOR AI INFERENCE (9 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Together Compiler is a truly continual optimization loop that leverages high-throughput agents to optimize for diverse inference workloads.

kept.heading: WEB GROUNDING FOR THE DECISIONS API (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Perplexity's Decisions API can now search the web before it answers.

kept.heading: KIMI-K3.1-PRO (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Kimi K3.1 Pro, the latest in the 3T-class models, excels in multimodal tasks, improving outputs in coding, 3D creation, and factual accuracy with a million-token context window.

kept.heading: YOU DON'T NEED LONG CONTEXT (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Researchers find that frontier language models perform well with shorter contexts without sacrificing accuracy.
